//: dev-precompiled -- the dev world, booting from a PRE-COMPILED image instead of compiling ~470
sources in the browser. `./build_it_please.sh --profile dev-precompiled`.
WHY IT EXISTS, measured (docs/measurements/boot-timing-2026-07-31.md): the compile-at-boot dev
index.html reaches world-ready in 3219 ms, of which 97% is compiling -- all 22 source files are
fetched within 103 ms. The same tree built pre-compiled reaches it in 59 ms. That is 55x, and
nothing is given up: same parts, same three entry pages, every class present.
THE TRADE, also measured: the pre-compile driver adds a headless boot-and-harvest to the build,
12.2 s -> 17.5 s (+5.3 s), against -3.16 s per page load. Break-even is under TWO reloads per
build. Arc 5 (PR-D5) declined a pre-compiled `dev` on exactly this ground -- 'worth paying once
per shipped artifact and not once per iteration' -- but weighed only the cost, because the
saving had never been measured. This profile does not overrule that decision: `dev` is
untouched and stays the default, so the inner loop pays nothing and this is opt-in for the
sessions that reload the page more than they rebuild.
⚠ sources: "lazy" rather than "background", for two reasons. It matches production, so the
one artifact shape that is heavily gated is also the shape this one has; and `background`
fetches core's eager batches BEHIND the running world, which the boot smoke's per-part counter
cannot distinguish from a lazy part dragging them in (it reported exactly that false positive
on the first spike). Inspectors still work -- they await the layer, which is what `lazy` means.
⚠⚠ index.html ONLY, AND THAT IS FORCED -- not a simplification. A pre-compiled image is
harvested by booting ONE page, and the image then contains exactly the classes that page loads.
index.html does not load lazy parts, so the image lacks them (48 classes today) -- which is
precisely what makes a lazy part cheap. But index-sw.html and worldWithSystemTestHarness.html
preset FIZZYGUM_EAGER_ALL_PARTS, so on those pages the reflective layer ingests EVERY part's
sources, and ingest-only mode does `window[name].class = @` (src/meta/Class.coffee) against a
class the image never defined -> 'Cannot set properties of undefined (setting class)'. MEASURED,
not theorised: shipping all three entries produced exactly that, twice, on index-sw.html.
ONE IMAGE CANNOT SERVE TWO PAGES WITH DIFFERENT EAGERNESS. Production dodges this by shipping
index.html alone; so does this profile.
⇒ THE SUITE DOES NOT RUN ON THIS TREE, and does not need to: `dev` stays the default and stays
compile-at-boot, so the suite, the gauntlet and every capture keep running exactly as before.
This profile is for the human who opens index.html and drives the world by hand.
